summary.headline: The Tricentennial Committee approved two new members and refined budgets for major 2027 anniversary events including a drone show and parade.
summary.summary: The Tricentennial Committee voted to approve the appointments of Amy Van Nest and Therese Ricard to help organize Southborough's upcoming 300th anniversary celebration. Members reviewed an overall event budget projection of approximately $224,400 out of an anticipated $250,000 fundraising target, while planning outreach efforts for Heritage Day and townwide mailings for the commemorative brick fundraiser. The committee also received detailed status updates on the New Year's Day 2027 drone show contract, commemorative utility pole banners, the time capsule project, and school district involvement.

topics.title: House Tour update
topics.summary: Organizers reported on preparations for the tricentennial house tour scheduled for September 18, 2027, from 12:00 p.m. to 3:00 p.m. The committee discussed logistics, volunteer docent recruitment, and budgeting.
key_details: Nine homes and two garden-themed properties are currently committed, with an ultimate goal of 10 to 12 stops.
Specific addresses and home details will be kept confidential and teased closer to the event date.
The event will require at least 20 volunteer docents to staff properties and allow volunteers time to tour.
A proposed budget line item of $5,000 will cover passport booklets, signage, and required public safety details.
Local bakeries and garden centers will be approached to provide small incentives or gifts for host homeowners.
topics.outcome: Discussion only; volunteer recruitment and local business partnerships will proceed.

topics.title: Committee appointments for new volunteers
topics.summary: The committee interviewed two candidates who had been conditionally appointed by the Select Board the previous evening. Both residents shared their professional backgrounds and volunteered to help manage logistics and budgeting.
key_details: Amy Van Nest shared her corporate operations, process management, and logistics background.
Therese Ricard shared her background as a CPA, controller, and risk manager with strong financial and budgeting expertise.
Both candidates agreed to lead or support working groups for upcoming events.
topics.outcome: Committee voted unanimously to approve the appointments of Amy Van Nest and Therese Ricard.

topics.title: Fundraising and event budget review
topics.summary: The committee reviewed anticipated revenue and preliminary budget allocations across all planned anniversary events. Members emphasized the necessity of capping individual event expenses and accounting for mandatory police and fire details.
key_details: Anticipated fundraising total is approximately $250,000, with $175,000 currently committed by sponsors.
Preliminary event budget line items total $224,400 across all scheduled activities.
Major projected expenses include $75,000 for the parade, $35,000 for the First Day/drone show, $35,000 for the Music Festival, and $35,000 for the Firemen's Muster.
Public safety details must be budgeted directly within each event's allocation based on four-hour minimum blocks.
Event leads were asked to submit refined budget breakdowns and schedule estimates for the next meeting.
topics.outcome: Event chairs will submit refined line-item budgets and security hour estimates for review at the October meeting.
topics.why_it_matters: The committee manages hundreds of thousands of dollars in municipal allocations, donations, and sponsorships to stage anniversary events across the community.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The committee deferred approval of prior meeting minutes due to lack of a quorum of reviewing members, scheduled the next regular meeting, and adjourned.
key_details: Meeting minutes approval was postponed to the October meeting.
The next committee meeting was scheduled for Wednesday, October 14, 2026.
topics.outcome: The meeting adjourned at approximately 8:45 p.m.

topics.title: Street utility pole banners
topics.summary: Members reviewed progress on securing permits from utility companies to hang commemorative banners on street utility poles throughout Southborough's four villages. The committee approved banner visual designs and color contrast adjustments.
key_details: Verizon confirmed that commemorative tricentennial banners are permissible provided they contain no commercial advertising.
Banners will measure 18 inches by 36 inches and will be installed using bracket kits.
Each village will feature village-specific banners displaying a historical photo and village name.
The committee agreed to utilize blue banners with white lettering for maximum visibility and legibility from roadways.
topics.outcome: Staff will submit pole locations for utility approval and order sample test banner kits.

topics.title: Heritage Day planning and promotions
topics.summary: The committee organized staffing and booth activities for the upcoming Heritage Day celebration on Monday, October 12, at the St. Mark's field. The booth will promote tricentennial activities, sell merchandise, and accept orders for commemorative bricks.
key_details: Heritage Day runs October 12, with booth setup beginning at 9:30 a.m. and public hours from 10:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m.
Activities include handing out free popcorn, selling logo t-shirts, displaying banner samples, and accepting engraved brick orders.
Committee members established two volunteer shifts: 9:30 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. and 12:00 p.m. to 3:30 p.m.
Printed event calendars and volunteer signup sheets will be distributed to visitors.
topics.outcome: Volunteer shifts were filled and materials were organized for the October 12 event.

topics.title: First Day celebration and drone light show contract
topics.summary: Andrew Dennington reported on finalizing the town's contract with Firefly Drone Shows for the New Year's Day 2027 opening celebration. The committee reviewed scheduling, location planning, and programming ideas.
key_details: The contract with Firefly Drone Shows is priced at $25,000 for a 15-minute, 200-drone aerial light show.
The event is scheduled for the evening of Friday, January 1, 2027, on St. Mark's field, with a rain/snow date of Saturday, January 2.
Firefly will work with the committee to design custom Southborough imagery, including town historic landmarks.
Additional First Day activities include a town history presentation by author Nick Noble, morning yoga sessions, children's recreation, and a bonfire hosted by the Firefighters Association.
topics.outcome: Contract execution is anticipated within days; custom imagery planning will begin.
topics.why_it_matters: The drone light show serves as the high-profile opening event for Southborough's year-long tricentennial celebration.

topics.title: Time capsule and other event updates
topics.summary: The committee heard updates on the time capsule project, the commemorative tree planting program, and the Incorporation Day ceremony. Working group leads requested additional volunteer assistance.
key_details: Boy Scout Troop 1 has volunteered to assist with door-to-door collection of community items for the time capsule.
The time capsule will emphasize archival-quality photographic and written records and is planned for above-ground storage to prevent water damage.
Donated legacy trees for each village will be selected within six to eight weeks for spring 2027 planting alongside commemorative granite markers.
The official Incorporation Day ceremony is slated for Tuesday, July 6, 2027, at Heritage Park with a $2,000 budget.
topics.outcome: Committee members agreed to coordinate offline on time capsule item collection protocols.

topics.title: Marketing, outreach, and school coordination
topics.summary: Members discussed outreach strategies to inform the public and recruit volunteers, including direct mailings, newsletters, school communication channels, and tabling at the town transfer station. Coordination with local public schools has significantly expanded.
key_details: A commemorative brick fundraising postcard will be sent via Every Door Direct Mail to all 3,847 Southborough residential addresses.
Nonprofit postal authorization reduced the town's mailing cost from 25.9 cents to 11.49 cents per piece.
A committee outreach table will be set up at the Southborough Transfer Station on Saturday, September 27, from 12:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m.
Positive outreach responses were received from Woodward, Neary, Trottier, Finn, and Algonquin schools, opening avenues for student participation in the parade and historical projects.
topics.outcome: Outreach efforts will proceed across local media, the transfer station, and school networks.

votes.motion: Approve the appointments of Amy Van Nest and Therese Ricard to the Tricentennial Committee.
